designer.name: Nusrat Jahan Mim
designer.title: Wood & Metal Furniture Designer
designer.tagline: Crafting heirloom-quality furniture where warm timber meets forged steel.
designer.bio: I'm Nusrat — a furniture designer with five years of hands-on experience shaping solid hardwoods and raw metals into functional works of art. My practice sits at the intersection of traditional joinery and contemporary metalwork: every piece I build is designed to honor the natural grain of the wood while celebrating the strength and geometry of steel. I believe furniture should outlast trends, age beautifully, and tell a quiet story about the materials it's made from. When I'm not in the workshop, I'm sourcing reclaimed timber from old Dhaka buildings or sketching new joint details over cha.

experience.description: Managed the overall production system for corporate orders, handling everything from new product concepts and market research to final client handovers. Directed product development including 3D visualization, AutoCAD manufacturing drawings, CNC design, and knockdown drawing for multi-boring operations. Created SOPs, product BOM/BOQ, and ensured rigorous quality control during field measurements and project execution.
highlights: Led new product prototyping & customized corporate handling
Created SOPs, operation flowcharts & pricing models

experience.description: Supported architectural and structural design workflows using AutoCAD. Handled comprehensive project requirements including floor plans, elevations, sections, and detailed drawings for furniture, electrical, and plumbing systems.
highlights: Produced 3D models with 3ds Max/SketchUp & V-Ray renders
Conducted site visits & maintained strong client relationships

projects.title: Walnut & Blackened Steel Dining Table
projects.description: A statement dining table built for a growing family who wanted something they'd never replace. The 8-foot walnut slab is book-matched and finished with hand-rubbed tung oil, while the geometric steel base is blackened with beeswax to develop a living patina. Brass pins lock the top to the frame without visible fasteners.

projects.title: Reclaimed Teak Console
projects.description: Salvaged teak planks from a century-old riverboat were cleaned, re-sawn, and joined with traditional mortise-and-tenon joints to create a low console for a heritage apartment. The grain tells a story of decades of sun and monsoon — I simply cleaned it up and let the wood speak.

projects.title: Forged Iron Floor Lamp
projects.description: A sculptural floor lamp inspired by the branching forms of banyan roots. Each arm is drawn from a single bar of mild steel, forge-welded and textured at the anvil. The warm copper socket and natural linen shade soften the industrial silhouette for residential use.

projects.title: Live-Edge Mahogany Bench
projects.description: A sculptural entryway bench carved from a single slab of Chittagong mahogany. Butterfly keys in contrasting ebony stabilize a natural crack that runs the length of the piece, turning a flaw into a design feature. The tapered legs are shaped on the lathe and wedged through the seat.

projects.title: Powder-Coated Steel Shelving System
projects.description: A modular wall-mounted shelving system designed for a design studio's library. The matte-black steel frame uses a peg-and-slot system so shelves can be repositioned without tools. Smoked-glass shelves add visual lightness while brass pins provide warm accents at every connection point.

projects.title: Oak & Copper Bar Cart
projects.description: A mobile bar cart that pairs quarter-sawn white oak trays with a bent-copper frame. The copper was intentionally patinated with salt and vinegar to achieve an aged verdigris tone. Saddle-leather straps wrap the push handle and secure glassware during movement.

projects.title: Ash & Steel Rocking Chair
projects.description: A modern reinterpretation of the Windsor rocking chair with steam-bent ash spindles and a hand-woven jute seat. The rocker rails are fabricated from flat steel bar, creating a clean visual line that contrasts the organic curves of the wood. The geometry was prototyped in SolidWorks and refined over three full-scale mock-ups.

projects.title: Corten Steel Garden Table
projects.description: An outdoor dining table designed to embrace the elements rather than resist them. The Corten steel base develops a rich, protective rust patina over seasons, while the cast-concrete top is sealed to repel water. Stainless steel leveling feet keep everything stable on uneven garden ground.

process.title: Consultation & Sketches
process.description: Every project starts with a conversation. I sit down with the client to understand their space, their lifestyle, and how the piece will be used. Then I translate those needs into hand-drawn concept sketches — usually 3-4 directions to choose from.

process.title: CAD & Prototyping
process.description: Once we settle on a direction, I build a detailed 3D model in SolidWorks — refining proportions, testing joinery, and generating cut lists. For complex pieces, I build a scaled mock-up in cheap pine to test ergonomics before committing to the real material.

process.title: Material Sourcing
process.description: I hand-select every board and every steel section. For wood, that means visiting sawmills and reclamation yards across Dhaka and Chattogram, checking moisture content, grain, and character. Metals are sourced from trusted local suppliers I've built relationships with over the years.

process.title: Cutting & Joinery
process.description: This is where the workshop comes alive. Wood is milled, planed, and joined — mostly with traditional mortise-and-tenon or dovetail joints, reinforced where needed. Metalwork is cut, welded, and ground at the fabrication bench. Every joint is test-fitted dry before final assembly.

process.title: Finishing & Delivery
process.description: Wood surfaces are hand-sanded through progressively finer grits, then finished with oils, waxes, or lacquers depending on use. Metal is powder-coated, blackened, or left raw. The final piece is inspected, wrapped, and delivered to the client's space — often with a hand-written care guide.

faq.question: How long does a custom piece take?
faq.answer: Most commissions take 6–10 weeks from initial consultation to delivery. Simpler pieces like shelving or side tables can be ready in 3–4 weeks, while large dining tables or complex hybrid designs may take up to 12 weeks. I'll give you a realistic timeline at our first meeting.

faq.question: What areas do you deliver to?
faq.answer: I deliver anywhere within Dhaka city and can arrange white-glove delivery across Bangladesh. For international clients, I work with a trusted freight partner who handles crating and shipping. Delivery within Dhaka is included; outside Dhaka, shipping is quoted separately.

faq.question: Can I choose my own wood species or metal finish?
faq.answer: Absolutely — material selection is a collaborative process. I'll walk you through what's available, what works best for your use case, and what fits your budget. I keep a rotating inventory of walnut, teak, mahogany, ash, and oak, and can source specialty species on request.

faq.question: How do I care for my furniture?
faq.answer: Each piece ships with a custom care guide. Generally: dust with a soft cloth, avoid direct sunlight and heat sources, re-oil wood surfaces every 6–12 months with the same finish I used, and wipe metal with a dry cloth. I offer a free annual touch-up service for the first two years.

faq.question: What's your pricing like?
faq.answer: Pricing depends on size, materials, and complexity. A simple solid-wood side table starts around ৳25,000, while a full dining table with a steel base typically ranges from ৳80,000 to ৳1,50,000. I provide a detailed quote after our first consultation — no surprises.

faq.question: Do you take on commercial projects?
faq.answer: Yes — I've furnished cafés, design studios, and co-working spaces. For commercial work, I can produce small batches (up to 10–15 identical pieces) and work with your architect or interior designer on specifications. Volume pricing is available for larger orders.
